wind.status: NEW 2026-10-19 (owner: there was no wind noise; the sound heard as wind was the tyre layer). Every number is [AS] unless stated. 2026-10-21: interior slope 40 dB per decade (was 50).
wind.level_note: What the driver hears is the wind noise INSIDE the cabin. Outside, flow noise over a body is a dipole/boundary-layer source growing 50-60 log10 U (Lighthill 1952: dipole U^6; Hucho, Aerodynamics of Road Vehicles: 50-60 log10 U), but the cabin's glass and seals attenuate more as the spectrum moves up with the airspeed, so the interior level grows less steeply: about 40 dB per decade [AS] (12 dB per doubling; passenger cars read roughly 65 dBA at 100 km/h and 76 dBA at 200 km/h in total). Was 50 (owner 2026-10-21: the wind scaled too aggressively). rms_at_reference is the 100 km/h level, unchanged; tyre noise (35 dB per decade) still dominates in town; the two layers are now equally loud at about 200 km/h (was 130).
wind.centre_note: Strouhal-type scaling f = St * U / L: the spectrum's weight moves up proportionally with the airspeed
